page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.metal is a general-purpose, bare-metal server powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor built on x86_64 architecture. It delivers 48 physical cores and 96 virtual CPUs with dedicated resource allocation, supported by 384 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and high-capacity baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. Hardware instruction sets feature AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES cryptography, and virtualization flags, accessible directly without hypervisor intervention.

Performance benchmarks highlight strong multi-core processing capabilities and memory throughput. Multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU scores, software compilation workloads with Clang, and database operation benchmarks all perform in the top 25% of evaluated servers. Redis SET operations reach 77.66 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 48.44 GB per second. Conversely, single-core metrics across stress-ng, Geekbench, and bzip3 decompression fall within average performance ranges.

Tradeoffs are evident in artificial intelligence workloads: LLM text generation speed ranks in the lower percentiles due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. However, the high resource density of 96 vCPUs combined with fast local storage and massive network throughput makes this instance qualitatively cost-efficient for heavy concurrent processing. The hardware profile is optimized for large relational and non-relational database management, web serving clusters, parallel software compilation, and core enterprise application workloads.

Benchmark results show strong multi-threaded CPU output, high memory bandwidth, and elevated scores in database operations, software compilation, and static web serving. While single-threaded processing and LLM text generation show average to lower relative throughput due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators, its resource density and integrated storage make it well-suited for high-throughput enterprise applications, database hosting, web serving, and software compilation tasks.
